title: Approximation and Estimation
tagline: Year 4 — Rounding sensibly, bounding answers and estimating roots, percentages and products when options are far apart

introduction.overview: When the options of a question are far apart you do not need an exact answer; you need a close one, quickly. Approximation replaces numbers by nearby round ones, uses benchmark percentages, and bounds an answer between two easy values. The skill lies in choosing the precision: round more when options are spread, less when they are close.
introduction.placementRelevance: Timed tests reward approximation on arithmetic-heavy items, especially in data interpretation and simplification.
introduction.realWorldContext: Estimating costs, distances and quantities quickly is a daily workplace skill.

learningObjectives: Round to two significant figures safely
Bound an answer between two known values
Judge the precision needed from the options

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Relative error ≈ (rounded − exact) ÷ exact. Rounding both numbers of a product in opposite directions partly cancels the error.

coreDefinitions: Approximation: replacing a number by a nearby simpler one.
Significant figures: digits that carry the value (4,180 has 3 or 2).
Bounding: placing an answer between a lower and upper estimate.
Benchmark: an easy percentage or fraction to compare against.
Option spacing: the gap between answer choices.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: If the options are 10% apart, an error of 2% is harmless; if they are 1% apart, estimate more carefully or compute exactly.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Round to two figures, compute, compare with options. If two are close, tighten the rounding or calculate exactly.

mainNarrative: 4,180 × 52 ≈ 4,200 × 50 = 210,000; the exact value is 217,360. The difference is about 3%, safe if options are more than 5% apart.
A growth from 4,180 to 4,970 is about 800 ÷ 4,200 ≈ 19%.
If options are 24%, 25% and 26%, rough rounding is not enough; calculate exactly.

deepDiveAspects.title: Linear approximation for roots
deepDiveAspects.content: √(a² + d) ≈ a + d/(2a) for small d.

deepDiveAspects.title: Cancelling rounding errors
deepDiveAspects.content: Round numerator down and denominator down by the same percentage to keep a ratio the same.

solvedExamples.title: Growth
solvedExamples.question: Revenue rose from 4,180 to 4,970. Estimate the percentage growth.

shortcutMethods.title: Round, bound, compare

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Round to two figures, bound with easy values, and compare with the option spacing.

rulesForApplication: Tighten only if options are close.

placementTips.recruiterInsight: The nearest option to a good estimate is usually correct.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I tell when to be exact?
